Tokenized assets on the XRP Ledger, excluding stablecoins, averaged $5.2 billion, up 37% from Q2 and nearly 15-fold year-over-year.
Ledger’s order-book trading volume surged 180% year-over-year in Q3 of 2026, with larger transactions and fewer participants signaling a potential shift toward institutional adoption.
Daily order-book volume increased 26% quarter-over-quarter while daily decentralized exchange volume jumped 96% year-over-year to 5.16 million XRP.
The 10 largest accounts controlled 65% of order-book volume, up from 33% a year earlier.

In its Q3 XRP Liquidity report, Evernorth noted that larger orders, repeat traders and increased multi-signature adoption are consistent with professional market-making activity, although the identities of these accounts remain unverified.
Despite weaker cryptocurrency prices, XRP Ledger demonstrated relative resilience.
Dollar-denominated on-chain exchange volume declined 15% year-over-year, compared with a 42% contraction across seven major blockchain networks.
The ledger also processed 203.2 million transactions, up 13% year-over-year, despite a 34% decline in daily active accounts.
The key test heading into Q4 is whether institutional-scale trading attracts a broader participant base or liquidity remains concentrated among a handful of large accounts.
